title: Late onset necrotizing enterocolitis in infants following use of a xanthan gum-containing thickening agent
authors: Beal J, Silverman B, Bellant J, Young TE, Klontz K
population: Infants reported to the US Food and Drug Administration adverse event system who developed necrotising enterocolitis after a xanthan gum-containing feed thickener; 21 of 22 preterm, median gestational age 30.5 weeks
funder: not readable. The full text is behind a paywall and no open copy was located; the PubMed record lists no grant support. The corresponding author is affiliated with the Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, US Food and Drug Administration.
result: Adverse event reports submitted to the US Food and Drug Administration suggested a possible association between necrotising enterocolitis and ingestion of a commercial feed thickener by premature infants; review in 2011 of 22 cases with exposure revealed a distinct illness pattern. As quoted by EFSA in 2023: the thickener was used for gastro-oesophageal reflux or dysphagia in every case; 21 of 22 infants were preterm with a median gestational age of 30.5 weeks; it was consumed for a median of 13 days (range 1 to 31) before onset; 19 developed necrotising enterocolitis after 37 weeks post-menstrual age; 14 required surgery and 7 died; the daily intake was not recorded. The abstract was read in PubMed and the case details in the EFSA 2023 opinion, which quotes this report.
